added_lines: ardmore parish | 25 october 2026 steelstown parish newsletter thirtieth sunday in ordinary time 25 october 2026 year a gospel reflection | matthew 22:34–40 in today’s gospel, jesus teaches that the greatest c ommandment is to love god wholeheartedly and to love our neighbour as ourselves. these two responsibilities are inseparable and form the foundation of christian life. loving god involves more than religious practices suc h as prayer, worship, and scripture reading. it means trusting him in difficult times, remaining faithful through challeng es, choosing what is right, and allowing him to guide every aspect of our lives. genuine love for god is shown not only in words but also in daily actions. our love for god becomes visible in how we treat othe rs. we cannot truly love god while harming, judging , or refusing to forgive those around us. instead, we are called to show compa ssion, kindness, patience, and mercy. even simple acts such as listening, encouraging, forgiving, and helping those in need become powerful expressions of god’s love. jesus also calls us to recognise the dignity and worth of every person, including those who differ from us or disappoint us. true love does not ignore wrongdoing, but it speaks the truth with respect and sets boundaries without hatred. the central message of this gospel is that love must be at the heart of both our relationship with god and our relationship with others. faith is not measured by religious knowledge or activities alone, but by whether it transforms us into more loving people. when love guides our thoughts, words, and actions, our lives become a living witness to god’s presence in the world. prayer for the week may the lord bless us with hearts open to love. may he help us to see christ in one a nother and to bring kindness, hope, and compassion wherever we go. sunday readings | 1 november – all saints first reading: revelation 7:2–4, 9–14 psalm: 24:1–2, 3–4, 5–6 second fr micheál mcgavigan pp – fr roni zacharias cc – fr stephen ward cc sunday 25th october 2026 – thirtieth sunday in ordinary time – year a in this sunday’s gospel, jesus gives us the two great commandments: love god and love our neighbour. but there are two words we can easily overlook: “love your neighbour as yourself.” jesus does not tell us to put ourselves first, but neither does he tell us that we do not matter. christian love means learning to see ourselves as god sees us, with honesty, patience and mercy. we all have faults, regrets and things we would change, but none of these takes away our dignity or god’s love for us. perhaps learning to accept god’s mercy for ourselves also helps us to become more merciful towards others. we do not have to demand perfection from ourselves, and neither should we demand it from those around us. speak to yourself with the same kindness you would offer to somebody you love. you too carry the image of god. welcome to god’s family eoghan david o’carroll; grace anna mccauley; myles eamon doherty. requiescan t in pace we offer our sympathies to the family and friends of: michael deery, galliagh park; mary mcivor, carnhill; adrian gallagher, thorndale; martin concannon, richmond crescent; john duffy, kingsfort crescent; gerard davis, grainan drive; kevin harkin rossnagalliagh; colm mcguinness, fernabbey drive
